Title: Anwar: University students, institutions among 2027 Budget priorities
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: University students and higher education institutions will be among the key priorities in the 2027 Budget, which is currently being finalised, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the 2027 Budget would cover various sectors and segments of society, including farmers, fishermen and the Orang Asli, as well as technology and artificial intelligence (AI).
"God willing, university students and universities will certainly also be included in (the Budget). Hopefully, I will be able to deliver what I can within the limitations," he said in his speech at the 2026 Tokoh Siswa Negara Awards ceremony.
Also present were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, his deputy Adam Adli Abd Halim, and Higher Education Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Aminuddin Hassim.
Anwar, who is also the finance minister said the preparation of the 2027 Budget required careful consideration of requests from thousands of associations, hundreds of departments and dozens of ministries
"Everything is reasonable and rational. From the paddy fields in Kedah, fishermen in Terengganu, the Orang Asli, Iban longhouses in Sarawak, technology and AI, all are demanding attention," he said.
He said his busy schedule finalising the Budget had forced him to cancel almost all events scheduled for this week, except for certain events, including Formula 1 at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).
"I cancelled all the events, but I decided to proceed with tonight's event. For the university students, I felt that I wanted to attend," he said.
The 2027 Budget is scheduled to be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat on Oct 9. It will be the fifth Madani Budget.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: F&B operators encouraged to explore more cuts of Japanese Wagyu
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian food and beverage (F&B) operators are encouraged to explore a wider range of Japanese Wagyu cuts in their dishes to make the premium beef more accessible to consumers.
Japan External Trade Organisation (Jetro) Kuala Lumpur managing director Koichi Takano said most food operators currently preferred premium cuts such as tenderloin and sirloin, which were more commonly associated with steak dishes.
However, he said growing awareness of Japanese Wagyu among Malaysian consumers presented an opportunity to introduce new ways of enjoying the beef.
"More consumers in Malaysia are becoming familiar with Japanese Wagyu and we believe there is an opportunity to make it more accessible.
"By introducing more cuts to the food service industry, more people will be able to enjoy Japanese Wagyu in various ways, while allowing it to be served at a wider range of food establishments," he said after launching a B2B trade seminar here yesterday.
The seminar was organised by Jetro Kuala Lumpur together with halal-certified Japanese Wagyu supplier Zenrich Allied Sdn Bhd (Zenrich Wagyu) and Kurohana Wagyu Export Promotion Consortium to expand the use of Japanese Wagyu in the food sector.
Takano said Japanese Wagyu is now the largest single food and agricultural export category from Japan to Malaysia by value.
He said exports of Japanese Wagyu to Malaysia had also continued to grow year-on-year.
"This has made the Malaysian market increasingly important to producers and suppliers from Japan," he said.

Title: #NSTviral: Malaysian cooking oil, sugar spotted for sale in Narathiwat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian packet cooking oil and sugar have been spotted for sale at a market in Narathiwat, Thailand, raising questions over how the controlled goods ended up across the border.
The discovery was shared on Threads by user Hafeezboh, who claimed to have spotted Malaysian-made packet cooking oil and sugar while visiting a market in Narathiwat.
"Did we officially export this, or was it smuggled?" he asked.
The post drew attention from other social media users, with several suggesting that the goods may have been taken out of Malaysia illegally.
One user, Ahnaz8712, claimed that certain parties were taking advantage of the border area to make a profit, while Aliphjolie said subsidised goods should not be sold overseas.
Meanwhile, Keiko_13r claimed that Malaysian-made packet cooking oil had been spotted not only in southern Thailand but as far as the Philippines.
However, based on the post, it could not be determined whether the cooking oil and sugar found in Narathiwat had been legally exported or taken out of Malaysia through smuggling activities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johan Setia, Nilai record unhealthy air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10pm, with Johan Setia in Selangor recording the highest reading at 137.
The Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System showed Nilai in Negri Sembilan recorded the second-highest reading at 131.
A total of 60 other areas recorded moderate air quality, with API readings between 51 and 100, while six areas recorded good air quality, with readings between 0 and 50, out of 68 monitoring stations nationwide.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy and 300 and above hazardous.
The public, particularly those in affected areas, are advised to reduce outdoor physical activity and wear face masks where necessary to reduce health risks.

Title: Anwar urges Gen Z to reject wrongdoing, serve the people
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged Gen Z Malaysians to develop greater awareness and determination to serve the people and reject wrongdoing.
He said academic achievement alone was not enough, citing scandals involving 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB), Felda and Tabung Haji as examples of how education did not necessarily guarantee integrity or good character.
"Most of those involved are not from among the uneducated. Almost all of them are graduates. Some have master's degrees and PhDs.
"So education and knowledge alone do not guarantee noble character," he said in his speech at the National Student Icon Award 2026 at the Putrajaya Marriott Hotel today.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir was present.
Anwar said the younger generation should not be judged solely by academic achievement, but also by their willingness to bring about meaningful change.
"There must be a new spirit among Gen Z — a high level of awareness, and I believe an interest in serving and defending the people, embracing what is good and rejecting decay," he said.
He said student leaders should possess not only academic excellence but also determination, fighting spirit and a desire to bring change.
Anwar said education must also be grounded in faith, morality, character and a strong sense of identity.
"If education does not train us, if after three or four years at university there is no awareness to defend the plight of the people, no awareness to correct weaknesses, damage and decay in the system, then the system is not assured.
"This is a reminder to all of us," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar clears schedule to focus on 2027 Budget
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has cleared his schedule and cancelled several programmes this week to focus on finalising the 2027 Budget.
Anwar, however, said he made an exception for the National Student Icon Award 2026, as he considered the programme which involves student leaders important.
"I have actually cancelled all my programmes this weekend. The F1 event (Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix), I had to attend because Malaysia is co-hosting.
"But over these two or three days, I have cancelled everything because I am working hard to complete the budget," he said in his speech at the 2026 Tokoh Siswa Negara Awards Ceremony.
Present were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir and Deputy Minister Adam Adli.
Anwar said the government needs to take into account a wide range of demands and needs across sectors, ministries and states in preparing the budget.
"The budget involves the demands and needs of the people, thousands of associations, hundreds of departments and dozens of ministries.
"And all of them are reasonable and important. From the padi fields in Kedah, fishermen in Terengganu, Orang Asli communities, the Iban in Sarawak, to technology and AI, all require attention," he said.
Anwar said several programmes scheduled over the coming days would be attended by other ministers on his behalf as he remained focused on budget preparations.
"Tomorrow there is an international syariah conference, and the day after that, there is a youth assembly. I have asked other ministers to represent me.
"But I wanted to attend this student programme," he said.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government would also examine procurement and operating cost pressures faced by small businesses amid global supply disruptions when drawing up the 2027 Budget.
The 2027 Budget is scheduled to be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat on Oct 9.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five detained after RM1mil food, alcohol seizure in Subang Jaya
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Five people, including four Myanmar nationals, were detained after food and alcoholic beverage products worth more than RM1 million were seized in a raid in Subang Jaya.
Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence Investigation (WCB/PSK) commander of the Federal Internal Security and Public Order Department Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said the five were detained during Op Taring Alpha 5 at 11.30am.
He said four of the Myanmar nationals were believed to be working as supervisors and workers at the premises, while the other was the manager.
Acting on information, the operations team inspected the premises, which was suspected of being used to store, sell and distribute food products that did not meet requirements and approvals set by the authorities.
It found 118 types of food products and 23 boxes containing various types of liquid believed to be alcohol made in China and suspected of being subject to unpaid customs duties, he said in a statement.
Mohd Zaki said the total value of the seizure was estimated at RM1,022,635.20.
He said the integrated operation was conducted by the Bukit Aman WCB/PSK under the Department of Internal Security and Public Order, together with the Petaling District Health Office, Health Ministry, Customs Department and Subang Jaya City Council.
Police took action against the detained individuals under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, and those detained for immigration offences were handed over to the Subang Jaya district police headquarters Criminal Investigation Division investigating officer, he said.
The premises manager was also handed over to the Customs Department to assist investigations, he said.
Mohd Zaki said the Bukit Aman WCB/PSK had conducted 272 raids nationwide from Jan 1 to today.
He said 459 people were detained for various offences involving smuggling of untaxed goods, leakage of controlled and subsidised goods, wildlife smuggling and e-waste-related operations.
"During the same period, the total value of seizures recorded was estimated at RM331.72 million," he added.

Title: Selangor extends RM30 public transport subsidy to KTM Komuter
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor state government has expanded its RM30 public transport subsidy to KTM Komuter services, effective immediately.
State Investment, Trade and Mobility Committee chairman Ng Sze Han said the expansion would enable more users to benefit from the subsidy, which initially covered Rapid KL On-Demand and Kumpool services.
He said more than 90 per cent of subsidy recipients previously opted for Rapid KL On-Demand, with those aged 26 to 35 making up the largest user group at 35 per cent.
"By including KTM Komuter in the scheme, we aim to have a greater impact on the commuter community in Selangor and encourage wider use of the public transport network," he said in a statement.
The expansion is being implemented under the Selangor Resilience Package, an initiative aimed at easing the cost of living, particularly for workers and students who rely on public transport for their daily journeys.
The initiative is managed by Rantaian Mesra Sdn Bhd (RMSB), a subsidiary of Menteri Besar Selangor (Incorporated) (MBI Selangor), in collaboration with transport service providers and a digital payment platform.
The programme will run until December, with 50,000 subsidy quotas available.
Applicants must be registered voters in Selangor. Eligibility is determined based on voter registration status, rather than residential address or place of employment.
The subsidy covers KTM Komuter services in the Klang Valley and northern sectors, as well as the Southern Shuttle Service.
Eligible applicants can apply through the Nine application by selecting KTM Komuter as their preferred transport service.
Once approved, the RM30 monthly subsidy will be automatically credited to the user's Nine e-wallet.
Users can then purchase tickets or travel passes through the KTMB Mobile or KITS Style applications by selecting Nine as the payment method.
The state government urged eligible Selangor voters to apply promptly and make use of the subsidy to reduce their daily travel costs.

Title: 15-year-old boy drowns in Klang lake
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A 15-year-old boy drowned after going swimming in a lake in Bandar Botanik, Klang.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 6.21pm.
He said seven firefighters and a fire engine from the Andalas Fire and Rescue Station were sent to the scene, with the search assisted by the Shah Alam Water Rescue Team.
"The victim's body was found by the Water Rescue Team at 8.21pm," he said in a statement.
Ashrul Riezal said the victim's parents identified the body before it was handed over to the police. -- BERNAMA

Title: Terberg drives Malaysia-made tractors into global ports
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Terberg Tractors Malaysia Sdn Bhd has shipped more than 8,000 terminal tractors made in Johor to ports and logistics hubs in over 50 countries.
This has turned Terberg Tractors into a significant export base for the Dutch industrial vehicle maker Royal Terberg Group BV
Terberg Tractors is a 50:50 joint venture between Sime Darby Bhd's unit Sime Darby Industrial Sdn Bhd and Royal Terberg.
It has evolved from a local distributor established in 1999 into a manufacturing operation serving markets across the Asia Pacific, the Middle East, Africa and the Americas, according to Sime Darby.
Based in Pasir Gudang, Terberg Tractors has a facility with an annual production capacity of 1,000 units and employs more than 300 Malaysians.
Sime group chief executive officer Datuk Jeffri Salim Davidson said Terberg Tractors' growth demonstrated the potential of Malaysian manufacturing capabilities in producing specialised industrial vehicles for global markets.
"A Malaysian team in Pasir Gudang is building specialist industrial vehicles that port operators across the world rely on to keep their operations running, and that is something to be proud of," he said.
Terberg Tractors is also expanding into electric terminal tractors as global ports move towards lower-emission operations.
After launching its YT200EV in 2022, the company introduced the next-generation YT201EV in May 2026. More than 300 units have been sold globally to date.
It has also co-developed a new cabin design with Terberg Group in the Netherlands, which improves performance by 10 per cent while lowering construction costs.
The company has invested more than RM12 million since 2024 to strengthen its manufacturing capabilities, including a new blasting and painting shop, warehouse expansion and laser machinery.
Its integrated automated production line can assemble both diesel and electric terminal tractors, while its automatic blasting system is the first of its kind within the Terberg Group.
Terberg Tractors is also deepening its Malaysian supply chain, spending about RM100 million annually with more than 200 active local suppliers.
Local suppliers account for about half of its total materials spending and provide key components, including engines and transmissions.
Terberg Tractors is working to bring more Malaysian suppliers into Terberg's global supply chain for cabin and chassis production.
On the technology front, Terberg Connect, the group's telematics system, is installed on 7,000 Terberg units globally, allowing customers to monitor fleet performance and maintenance in real time.
Terberg Tractors is also working with strategic partners to develop autonomous terminal tractors, while investing in leadership and technical training to build a local talent pipeline for advanced manufacturing and engineering.

Title: 408 MCBA officers start on-site RTS Link training
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A total of 408 pioneer Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) officers have begun on-site training ahead of their deployment to the Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link entry point.
Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link Entry Point Commander Khairul Nizam Hashim said the New Officer Onboarding Programme held today was a continuation of basic training to strengthen their readiness before they are assigned to the field.
"The programme focuses on familiarising officers with their work environment and locations, understanding MCBA roles and responsibilities, and operating procedures, including standard operating procedures, inspections and communication.
"It also covers teamwork, discipline, integrity and ethics," he said in a statement.
He said the officers comprised 39 Assistant Border Superintendents and 369 Border Superintendent Assistants.
All of them underwent three months of basic training at the Segamat Police Training Centre before being deployed to prepare for work at the RTS Link entry point.
Khairul Nizam said the on-site programme was aimed at ensuring officers could apply the knowledge they had gained in an actual operational setting.
"Operational readiness continues to be strengthened through manpower deployment, inter-agency coordination, security, and a proactive enforcement approach based on intelligence, risk and technology," he said.
The RTS Link is due to begin operations on Jan 1, 2027.

Title: ECRL cables stolen three days in a row ahead of operations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The public should to stay away from the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) alignment following a series of cable theft and cable-cutting incidents in Selangor that could pose serious safety risks and disrupt ongoing testing and commissioning works.
China Communications Construction ECRL Sdn Bhd (CCCECRL) in a statement said the incidents occurred over three consecutive days from Sept 27 to 29 as the ECRL underwent testing and commissioning ahead of its targeted commencement of operations in December this year.
It said the ECRL alignment is an active testing area and is not open to the public, while railway systems, equipment, and cables along the alignment are either powered or undergoing live testing.
"Any unauthorised entry or interference with railway infrastructure therefore carries a serious risk of severe injury or electrocution," it said.
The company said cable theft and damage to railway infrastructure could also disrupt ongoing testing and commissioning works, as affected equipment would need to be inspected, repaired or replaced before testing could resume.
It said affected tests might also have to be repeated, adding that continued incidents could affect the project schedule and delay the planned commencement of operations.
CCCECRL has lodged police reports on recent incidents.
It also said security measures along the ECRL alignment have also been strengthened, with local authorities stepping up surveillance and monitoring in the affected areas as efforts continue to prevent further incidents and safeguard the ongoing testing and commissioning works.
"Anyone who notices suspicious people or activities along the alignment should report it immediately to the police or the nearest CCCECRL section office," it added.

Title: Woman trapped in SUV for 30 minutes after trailer crash
Article:
HULU SELANGOR: A woman was trapped in an SUV for nearly 30 minutes after it was involved in a collision with a trailer on the North-South Expressway.
The 32-year-old woman also suffered injuries to her hand and back in the 5.30pm incident at KM422.1 of the southbound expressway.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received a call at 5.34pm and firefighters arrived at the scene 16 minutes later.
"The accident involved a Proton X50 and a trailer. Upon arrival, we found the woman trapped in the SUV. Firefighters immediately assisted in freeing her.
"She was given treatment by firefighters before being taken to Sungai Buloh Hospital," he said.

Title: Pregnant motorcyclist loses baby in crash with SUV
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: A motorcyclist who was nine months pregnant lost her unborn baby in a two-vehicle crash at Km4.3 of Jalan Kota Tinggi-Kluang.
Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said police received information about the crash involving the 35-year-old woman, who was riding a SYM motorcycle, and a Nissan X-Trail SUV driven by a 61-year-old man, at 1.55pm.
"The accident is believed to have occurred when the SUV, which was entering a junction, collided with the victim's motorcycle travelling on a straight road.
"The victim sustained head injuries and internal bleeding, while her unborn baby was confirmed dead after an examination at Sultan Ismail Hospital," he said in a statement.
Yusof said the woman was receiving treatment at the hospital, while the SUV driver was uninjured.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

Title: Court overturns acquittal, health officer ordered to enter defence on unnatural sex charges
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today overturned a High Court decision acquitting a health officer of seven charges of having unnatural sex with a woman and ordered him to enter his defence.
A three-member bench chaired by Datuk Noorin Badaruddin allowed the prosecution's appeal against the Kota Baru High Court decision on Dec 10, 2025, which upheld the acquittal of Mohd Faris Helmi Ab Rahim, 38, on all seven charges under Section 377B of the Penal Code.
"The High Court's order upholding the decision of the Sessions Court is set aside. We find that a prima facie case has been established against the respondent (Faris) on the charges under Section 377B of the Penal Code. Therefore, the respondent is ordered to enter his defence.
"The case is remitted to the Sessions Court before another judge to enable the respondent to enter his defence in accordance with the law, and the case management date at the Pasir Mas Sessions Court is fixed for Oct 15," said Noorin, who sat with Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid.
On April 16, 2024, the Pasir Mas Sessions Court acquitted and discharged Faris after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against him. The decision was subsequently upheld by the Kota Baru High Court.
According to the seven charges, Faris was alleged to have intentionally unnatural sex with a 34-year-old woman, who was the owner of a bakery, in a car in front of a religious secondary school in Pasir Mas and at a petrol station in Salor.
The offences were allegedly committed between 5.30 pm on July 29, 2019 and 1 pm on Sept 18, 2021, under Section 377B of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
In her grounds of judgment, Noorin said the Sessions Court judge had erred in law by applying the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt at the close of the prosecution's case.
"By treating the question of consent or lack of consent as an element that the prosecution was required to prove under Section 377B, the Sessions Court judge erred in finding that the evidence of the first prosecution witness (the victim) was insufficient at that stage, when the evidence was not intrinsically incapable of belief, and the matters raised against her were matters that should properly be tested through the respondent's defence.
"We find that the High Court also failed to correct the error and instead upheld the Sessions Court's decision. Therefore, there are proper grounds for this court to intervene in the decisions of both courts," she said.
Noorin said the court found that the victim's evidence was direct evidence concerning the material acts forming the essence of the charges and was not evidence that was intrinsically incapable of belief.
"A witness's credibility may be challenged, but that does not mean the evidence is intrinsically incapable of belief.
"Whether the witness's evidence ultimately withstands proper scrutiny at the conclusion of the entire case is a matter that should be decided after the respondent has been given an opportunity to answer the prosecution's case," she said.
The proceedings were conducted by Deputy Public Prosecutor Noor Farhana Adham, while lawyer Siti Syaerah Meor Zulkefli 'Auni represented Faris.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Democratic wave hitting Republican states hardest, scrambling Senate strategy
Article:
KENTUCKY Democrats say they have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to flip a US Senate seat in a Republican stronghold. But a couple of things are missing: their governor and money.
Kentucky is one of several states that President Donald Trump won by double digits in 2024 where Republicans are significantly trailing the president's performance, an indication that Democrats have expanded their pathway to a majority in November's midterm elections.
It's not clear, however, that the party will invest its limited resources into flipping seats once considered to be out of reach.
The Democratic wave is crashing hardest in states Trump won by wide margins, though Republicans are also significantly underperforming in Georgia and North Carolina, where Trump won by 2 and 3 percentage points, respectively.
The volume of unexpectedly competitive states could scramble the final stretch of the campaign cycle as top officials assess where to spend their war chests.
"Not only is there a swing away from the Republican Party compared to 2024, but the swing actually seems to be somewhat bigger in red America than in blue America, and that's putting these states that Trump won easily very much into play," said David Hopkins, a political science professor at Boston College.
Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority and entered the political cycle with a favourable map to maintain control of the chamber for the final two years of Trump's presidency.
But less than five weeks out from Election Day, polling shows Democrats are competitive in 10 states Trump won by double digits in 2024: Ohio, Alaska, Iowa, Texas, Florida, Kansas, Nebraska, Mississippi, South Carolina and Kentucky.
To win the Senate, Democrats must defend two seats in states Trump carried and win four Republican-held seats, including at least two in states Trump won by double digits.
Ohio, Alaska, Iowa and Texas have largely been viewed as Senate battlegrounds this cycle, but the political environment is so poor for Republicans that Democrat Adam Hamilton is narrowly leading US Senator Roger Marshall in recent polls in Kansas, which Trump won by 16 percentage points.
[[nid:1545713]]
Democratic candidates Angie Nixon of Florida and Annie Andrews of South Carolina are running neck and neck against Republican incumbents in recent polls, which show Democratic-aligned candidates in Nebraska, Mississippi and Kentucky trailing by single digits.
Trump carried those states by margins ranging from 13 in Florida to 31 in Kentucky. He told reporters on Monday that "the polls are fake."
Polls capture voter sentiments but don't necessarily predict election outcomes. Several primary polls, for example, showed Francesca Hong leading by 20 or more points in the Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor. She lost by less than one per cent.
Democrat Charles Booker's internal polling has him within single digits of US Representative Andy Barr in the race to succeed longtime Republican US Senator Mitch McConnell of Kentucky.
But Barr has a US$2 million cash advantage over Booker, whose allies say Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear, a potential 2028 presidential candidate, could give him the boost he needs to win.
"We have a shot here in Kentucky to flip this seat, and we need to do it now," said Pamela Stevenson, minority floor leader of the Kentucky House.
Eric Hyers, Beshear's 2019 and 2023 campaign manager who helps run his In This Together PAC, said the governor has already endorsed Booker.
"They'll likely be together at get-out-the-vote events down the homestretch of the campaign," Hyers said.
Political prognosticators have shifted some races toward Democrats in deeply Republican states, but many of these expansion seats maintain ratings that view them as solidly Republican or likely to remain Republican.
The White House is deploying Trump to these states in an apparent effort to juice base turnout in November.
The president held a midterm rally in South Texas on Wednesday and will campaign in Ohio on Saturday and Nebraska on Monday.
Trump won Ohio by 11 points, Texas by 14 and Nebraska by 21.
His approval rating has fallen to a historic low of 32 per cent, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll, while his war with Iran and tariffs have driven up prices as voters have consistently highlighted the cost of living as their top concern ahead of the midterms.
That likely makes him more of a liability than an asset in traditional battlegrounds, political analysts say.
Democrats say they have transformed the map of races in play.
"Our goal has always been a Democratic Senate majority, and the pathways to get there have only gotten bigger since the start of the cycle," said Lauren French, a spokesperson for Senate Majority PAC, a Democratic super PAC. Super PACs can raise and spend unlimited sums but cannot coordinate with candidates, campaigns or party committees.
[[nid:1545712]]
French said Republicans have diverted resources from Georgia and North Carolina to Republican strongholds, where she said Republicans are starting to talk about gas prices and other costs.
While some Republicans have leaned into culture war issues such as transgender athletes in girls' and women's sports, other Republicans have begun distancing themselves from the Trump administration.
That includes Republicans in states such as Kansas and Mississippi, where US Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith acknowledged in a social media video last week that fuel cost was her constituents' top issue.
"I feel it, too, every time I fill up my truck to get around the state," she said. "This administration is working to end the conflict of Iran, which will ultimately lower the price of fuel."
Republicans are already outspending Democrats by millions of dollars - tens of millions in some cases - on future ad reservations in Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Alaska and Kansas, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact.
Republicans in reach states - Republican strongholds that could flip to Democrats in a wave election - also have significant financial advantages over their opponents, with the exception of South Carolina, where Andrews entered July with more than US$4 million on hand.
US Senator Darline Graham, who was appointed to the seat in July after the death of her brother US Senator Lindsey Graham, won the Republican nomination in an August special primary runoff but reported having just US$250,000 as of Aug 5.
Rufus Gifford, former finance chair for Joe Biden's and Kamala Harris' presidential campaigns, said there are strategic advantages to Democrats investing in expansion states, such as forcing Republicans to play defence in areas they didn't expect.
"The truth is that many of these states have been fool's gold for Democrats for a very, very long time," he said. But "there's very little doubt that we have a shot in some of these even more reach states."
* The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Govt to strengthen governance, curb leakages and abuse of power
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will continue to strengthen public service governance and integrity to curb leakages of public funds and abuse of power, particularly involving Federal Statutory Bodies, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the matter was among the issues discussed at the Special Cabinet Committee on National Governance (JKKTN) meeting, which he chaired today.
"I stresed that law enforcement must be accompanied by the continuous cultivation of integrity and good governance in the public and private sectors, as well as in society," he said in a Facebook post.
He said the meeting also agreed to conduct a legal study to formulate the policy and governance direction for a proposed Charities Bill to regulate trust entities and public funding.
He said the move was crucial to ensure entrusted funds were managed transparently and responsibly.
Anwar added that the meeting also agreed to the proposed implementation of the 'Cultivation of Public Service Values'.
On another matter, he said, the policy for the Statutory Bodies and Controlled Entities (Financial Governance) Bill would be presented to the cabinet this year to strengthen discipline and accountability in financial management.
"The meeting also agreed to the seven resolutions presented at the Fifth National Level Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption Research Conference on Sept 25," he said.
Anwar said the Madani government would continue to strengthen public service integrity and close avenues for leakages and abuse of power.
"Every ringgit of public money is a trust from the people that must be safeguarded, and every power granted must be used to guarantee their wellbeing," he added.

Title: Hengyuan brings back former CEO Ranta
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd has reappointed former chief executive officer (CEO) Erkki Tapio Ranta to lead the oil refiner effective today.
Ranta, 62, replaces Yin LuJiang, 55, who has stepped down as CEO after nearly three years in the role.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Hengyuan said Ranta joined Hengyuan International Sdn Bhd as a senior officer in November 2019 before becoming CEO in March 2020.
He served as the company's CEO until July 2021.
Ranta has more than 30 years of experience in the oil and gas industry.
After leaving Hengyuan in 2021, the Finnish national served as managing director of Germany-based Bayernoil Raffineriegesellschaft mbH until November 2024.
He was then an independent consultant in Croatia until August this year.

Title: Company manager remanded over alleged RM200m tax reduction fraud
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has remanded a company manager from a financial and corporate services agency for three days.
The man, in his 40s, is being investigated over allegations of submitting false documents to obtain a tax reduction worth about RM200 million.
Magistrate Illya Syaheedah Mohd Razif issued the remand order which is in force until Oct 3 following an application by the MACC at the Putrajaya magistrate's court
The suspect was arrested around 7pm yesterday when he appeared to provide his statement at the MACC headquarters.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect allegedly committed the offence between 2018 and 2026.
The suspect is also believed to have bribed an enforcement agency officer and manipulated about 480 company accounts using false documents to secure the tax reduction, while allegedly amassing wealth through the activities.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, confirmed the arrest and said the case was being investigated under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IOI Properties snaps up Shenton House for RM696mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IOI Properties Group Bhd is taking full ownership of Shenton House in Singapore through the acquisition of its owner, Shenton 101 Pte Ltd, for RM696.43 million.
IOI Properties said its unit Boulevard View Pte Ltd will buy 100 per cent of Shenton 101 from group chief executive officer and major shareholder Datuk Lee Yeow Seng.
The shares will be bought for just S$1 (RM3.21), but IOI Properties will also repay about S$217.06 million (RM696.43 million) that Lee had advanced to Shenton 101 as at July 31.
Shenton House, located at 3 Shenton Way in Singapore's central business district, is a 25-storey commercial building that is more than 50 years old.
IOI Properties plans to redevelop the site into a 35-storey mixed-use development with Grade-A offices, retail space and a 165-room luxury hotel.
The proposed development is expected to have a net lettable area of about 36,528 square metres and an estimated gross development value of S$1.61 billion (RM5.16 billion).
The redevelopment is estimated to cost S$973.65 million (RM3.12 billion), including construction costs, professional fees, financing costs and land-related charges.
Construction is expected to start in the first half of 2027 and be completed by the fourth quarter of 2031, subject to regulatory approvals.
IOI Properties said the project had received provisional permission from Singapore's Urban Redevelopment Authority in June, although written permission is still pending.
The company said taking full ownership of Shenton 101 will allow it to benefit from Shenton House's future profits and potential value increase, which it currently does not enjoy despite managing the redevelopment project.
Shenton House is also within walking distance of IOI Properties' IOI Central Boulevard Towers and Asia Square Tower 2.
This allows the company to build a larger property portfolio around Singapore's Marina Bay area.
The acquisition follows IOI Properties' decision in August 2024 to reject an earlier proposal by Lee to sell Shenton 101 to the company.
IOI Properties said its position had since changed, with IOI Central Boulevard Towers achieving more than 95 per cent committed occupancy and the company having strengthened its presence in Singapore through the acquisitions of South Beach and Asia Square Tower 2.
The acquisition will be funded using internally generated funds.
IOI Properties said its pro forma gearing would increase to 1.33 times from 1.29 times following the acquisition, while net gearing would rise to 1.10 times from 1.03 times.
The transaction is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to several conditions, including lender and regulatory approvals.
Lee, who is the vendor, and his brother Lee Yeow Chor, a major shareholder and director of IOI Properties, did not take part in the board's deliberations or voting on the transaction.

Title: Anwar, Bahrain Crown Prince discuss F1 preparations
Article:

Title: Nepal rescuers recover eight bodies after Himalayan avalanche
Article:
KATHMANDU: Rescuers recovered eight more bodies on Thursday from the area of a Himalayan avalanche that buried 16 expedition workers, in one of the worst mountain disasters in recent years.
The avalanche swept through the base camp of the 7,126-metre Himlung peak early on Sunday, as Nepali workers were preparing for later expeditions on the mountain located near the Chinese border.
"The team have found eight bodies today," said Tul Singh Gurung, president of the Nepal National Mountain Guide Association, taking the total to 15, with one person still missing.
"We are hopeful the last person will be found too," he added.
A team of eleven rescuers, including experienced guides, were at the site, digging through more than four metres of snow which had buried tents at the base camp.
The bodies of two mountain guides were recovered on Sunday, and those of two kitchen staff were pulled out on Monday, followed by another three bodies on Tuesday.
Nepal's worst mountaineering disasters in recent years occurred in 2014, when an avalanche killed 16 people on Everest, and in 2015, when an earthquake killed 18 people, also on Everest.
Authorities are still searching for bodies from devastating floods sparked by a mountain glacial collapse on August 26 that killed more than 1,400 people and left over 5,000 missing.
Heavy rain since Thursday has triggered more floods and landslides, killing at least 21 people, according to the national disaster agency.
Home to eight of the world's 14 highest peaks, Nepal relies heavily on mountaineering and trekking tourism.
Himlung, where Sunday's avalanche occurred, is a popular destination for mountaineers looking to begin climbing 7,000-metre peaks.

Title: F1 Bahrain GP: Vehicles must pass five checks before entering Sepang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Vehicles heading to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) for the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix tomorrow will have to pass through five designated screening points before being allowed into the circuit grounds.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the checks would cover tickets, vehicle passes and access stickers.
"To ensure orderly access control, all vehicles heading to SIC are required to undergo screening at five main locations.
"All vehicles heading to SIC will be screened, with checks on tickets, vehicle passes and access stickers before visitors are allowed to enter the SIC grounds," he told a press conference at the Selangor police contingent headquarters.
The five screening points are the Chicken Hut area from the KLIA Toll Plaza direction; the route from KLIA Terminal 1 towards the KLIA mosque roundabout; the area before the roundabout; the route from Kompleks Warisan Rohaniah; and the four-way junction at the police quarters.
Shazeli said vehicles without access or parking passes, including motorcycles would not be allowed to enter SIC and would instead be directed to designated shuttle bus stops.
"Only authorised staff and workers with the relevant permits and passes will be allowed to enter on motorcycles," he said, adding that 4,000 parking spaces had been provided for the race.
He said 365 officers and personnel from the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department had been deployed for traffic control, congestion prevention patrols, law enforcement and VIP movement control throughout the event.
"Traffic control and enforcement will be carried out from 9am to 6pm daily, with traffic expected to peak on Sunday.
"Road users are advised to follow the instructions of personnel on the ground and plan their journeys in advance to ensure smooth traffic flow," he said.
Shazeli said summonses and towing action would be taken against vehicles parked on road shoulders and obstructing traffic.
"Passengers heading to KLIA) Terminals 1 and 2 are also urged to depart earlier to avoid congestion.
"This is to ensure they arrive at the airport on time," he said.
About 200,000 spectators are expected to attend the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at SIC from tomorrow until Sunday, with the highest attendance expected on race day.
SIC previously hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix from 1999 to 2017 before the race was dropped from the F1 calendar due to rising hosting costs and licensing fees.
F1 returns to Sepang this weekend with the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix, which was relocated to Malaysia after the original Bahrain race was unable to take place amid geopolitical tensions in West Asia.

Title: Smouldering bins, halted trams as French pupils protest
Article:
PARIS: A high school entrance hall caught fire in one French city and teenage protesters blocked trams in another on Thursday, as secondary pupils upped their strike over what they denounce as poor learning conditions.
The movement in the lycees, which students aged 15 to 18 attend for their final three years of secondary education in France, has seen hundreds detained in recent days.
Since last week, pupils have staged protests outside schools over grievances ranging from timetables, class sizes and a shortage of teachers to overheated classrooms during this year's heatwaves.
The protests have spread across the country from the Paris suburbs, with the government accusing hard-left politicians of encouraging the unrest.
Riot police were deployed to confront the students, with the force launching internal probes after accusations of brutality against three pupils, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez.
Some 340 demonstrations were underway in front of high schools mid-morning, with more than 160 establishments shut down as a result, police said.
University students joined in on Thursday, blocking physical access to around 30 campuses, including in Paris and the southern city of Marseille, a student union said.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu urged all ministers to postpone any travel nationwide, a source close to him said, so local authorities could "focus their resources on managing" the protests.
[[nid:1545678]]
In the northwestern city of Nantes, firefighters had to intervene to put out a fire in the entrance of a high school "following a gathering marked by violence towards staff", the regional education board said.
Regional authorities reported "acts of violence near high schools", mainly in Nantes, blaming "violent individuals" who "join the students to carry out acts of vandalism."
In the northeastern city of Strasbourg, authorities ordered trams to grind to a halt to "restrict the movements of rioters and demonstrators", the regional prefect said.
Raphael, a 17-year-old who did not give his surname for fear of reprisals, was among the protesters outside a school in Strasbourg, where some used barriers to obstruct the nearby tramway tracks.
"There are 35 of us per classroom. With 35C in summer, it's unbearable. There aren't enough toilets, and there are water leaks in some rooms," Raphael said.
"The building is falling apart, the cafeteria is too small. There's zero budget, zero resources, not enough supervisors," he said.
Nearby, students took photos of themselves in front of burning rubbish bins, holding up the sign with their school's name ripped off the tram stop.
Most pupils did not take part in the clashes that followed, instead breaking out into a sprint down the avenue when the police fired tear gas.
In the northern city of Lille, AFP reporters saw young people wearing black hoodies destroy the glass of a bus stop. Firefighters intervened to put out the flames on upturned dustbins set on fire.
The government has accused the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party of encouraging the protests.
But LFI's candidate for the 2027 presidential election, Jean-Luc Melenchon, said on Wednesday that his party "called for non-violent methods of struggle."

Title: Hextar Capital secures RM60mil road contract in Sarawak

Title: Euro slides to 17-month low, hit by rates and inflation mix
Article:
LONDON: The euro hit its lowest point in 17 months on Thursday, as investors battered European assets in light of the impact on the regional economy from higher oil prices and inflation, while mounting political uncertainty added to an uncertain backdrop.
The European currency fell below US$1.13 for the first time since May 2025 against the dollar, which has been in ascendance for the past couple of months, thanks in part to the largest quarterly rise in Treasury yields since 1994.
The euro also sank against the yen and the Swiss franc, and barely held in positive territory against the pound, as yields on French debt, which has been hounded by worries about France's shaky finances, surged to another 14-year high. And even benchmark German debt came under fire.
The euro was last down 0.35 per cent at US$1.1291. It declined nearly 2.5 per cent in September, its largest monthly decline since July 2025.
Europe is facing a range of political uncertainties as well, with a hotly contested French election next year, as well as increasing pressure on Germany's chancellor after a series of gains by the far-right AfD party in regional elections.
Data on Wednesday showed US inflation rose less than expected in August, along with downward revisions to July's figure, which lowered expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike this month.
But a surge in euro zone inflation underscored the threat that higher energy prices continue to pose to the global economy.
"This growth risk has been hanging over the euro," Rabobank head of FX strategy Jane Foley said.
"And despite the fact that the ECB was one of the first central banks in the G10 to hike interest rates, despite the fact that it's expected to go again, the euro hasn't been able to get traction."
"It's been bogged down by the fact that positions were very long and by this concern about (Europe) being an energy importer and then of course, at the margins certainly going into next year, you've got these political concerns."
European stocks fell 0.66 per cent, along with bond prices, adding to the drag on the euro.
The dollar clocked its sixth straight quarter of gains against a basket of currencies by the end of September, its longest such stretch since 2022 when US rates were rising more quickly than those elsewhere.
The dollar index was last up 0.31 per cent on the day, around its highest level since mid-May.
"The US dollar seems to be showing more sensitivity, just at the moment, to what's happening with say, 10-year Treasuries, than it is on pricing for when the next Fed rate hike might come," said Ray Attrill, head of FX strategy at National Australia Bank.
"While yields are continuing to rise for the time being, I think it's supportive for the dollar. If we do get an inflection point where it starts to really hurt the equity market, the dollar can benefit from that."
Global bonds suffered their largest monthly decline in years in September, pushing yields higher, due to a toxic mix of deteriorating government finances, a glut of issuance and rising inflation.
Sterling was down 0.3 per cent at US$1.322 after having slid 2.1 per cent last month, but was steady against the euro, which traded at its weakest point since late June against the pound, around 85.4 pence.
Against the yen, the dollar was up 0.5 per cent at 158.16 after falling 1.4 per cent against the Japanese currency last month, while the Australian dollar fell to a two-month low of US$0.6931 after domestic inflation came in below forecasts.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Federal Court sets five-day hearing for Petronas, Sarawak oil and gas petitions beginning Jan 25
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court has set five days from Jan 25 next year to hear petitions filed by Petroliam National Bhd (Petronas) and the Sarawak government challenging the state and federal laws governing oil and gas matters.
Judge Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang said the petitions would be heard in the order in which they were filed.
However, she left it to the Federal Court panel hearing the petitions to decide whether to first hear the Sarawak government's preliminary issue on the validity of the Sarawak (Alteration of Boundaries) Order in Council 1954 (OIC), which concerns the boundaries of Sarawak's territorial waters.
She said given the fact that the two petitions are not consolidated, the panel hearing the petitions would be in the better position to determine whether the preliminary issue should be heard first.
Rhodzariah made the decision today after the two cases came up before her for summonses for directions.
She also directed parties to file their respective submissions for the petitions as well as for the preliminary issues by Jan 11 and reply submissions by Jan 18, and she fixed Jan 12 for case management.
"The hearing date is fixed from Jan 25 until Jan 29, next year," she said.
Senior state counsel Mohd Adzrul Adzlan, who is representing the Sarawak government, informed the court that they will be filing an application with regard to their preliminary issue under Rule 23 of the Rules of the Federal Court 1995 within 14 days from today.
Meanwhile, both Petronas and the Sarawak government will write to the Chief Justice to request an enlarged panel of either a nine-man bench or an 11-man bench to hear the petitions.
Petronas and the Sarawak government had indicated to the court previously that they wanted their respective petitions to be heard separately.
Petronas wants its petition to be heard first, followed by the sequence in which the respective petitions were filed. However, the state government maintains that its petition should be heard first.
The national oil and gas company filed its petition on Jan 10 this year and obtained leave under Article 4 (4) of the Federal Constitution on March 16 this year, while the Sarawak government filed its petition on February 23.
In today's proceedings, Adzrul argued that the Federal Court panel hearing the petitions should first hear the preliminary issue concerning the OIC before proceeding to hear the petitions.
However, Petronas lawyer Datuk Dr Cyrus Das argued that there was no basis to have the legal status of the OIC determined as a preliminary issue and the OIC issue can be taken up in the course of hearing of the petition.
Senior Federal Counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly @ Arwi representing the federal government, supported the submission by Petronas's counsel, arguing that its (Petronas's) petition should be heard first.
Regarding Sarawak government's preliminary issue on the validity of the OIC, he said it was not necessary for the issue to be heard by way of a preliminary point of law and the state government can bring up the issue during the main hearing.
On March 16 this year, the Federal Court granted leave to the national oil and gas company to commence proceedings to challenge the legislative competency of the Sarawak State Legislature to enact certain laws and to declare several laws made by the Sarawak State Legislature invalid.
It claimed that the Sarawak state legislature lacked the competence to enact, modify, amend or revise law with respect to matters under List 1 of the Federal List in the Ninth Schedule of the Federal Constitution.
The Sarawak government, meanwhile, filed a petition against the government and Petronas, seeking the Federal Court to determine the constitutional validity and continued applicability of several federal Acts to Sarawak.
The state government, among others, is seeking a declaration that the Petroleum Development Act 1974 (PDA), the Continental Shelf Act 1966 and the Petroleum Mining Act 1966, as applied to Sarawak, were unconstitutional and void ab initio.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ajiya to dispose Puchong property for RM58mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ajiya Bhd's subsidiary, Ajiya Safety Glass Sdn Bhd (ASG) has inked a sale and purchase Agreement (SPA) with Esprit Care Sdn Bhd (ECSB) to dispose of a freehold industrial land in Puchong, Selangor for RM58 million.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, it said the proposed disposal comprises a single-storey factory and a two-storey office.
The land, located in Taman Perindustrian Puchong Utama, spans 1.35 hectares, with a gross built-up area of 9,839.52 square metres.
Ajiya said the disposal consideration was arrived at on a willing buyer-willing seller basis, taking into consideration the property's indicative market value of RM40 million, namely RM27 million for the land and RM13 million for the building, as assessed by CBRE WTW Valuation and Advisory Sdn Bhd.
It said the proposed disposal is expected to result in an estimated gross gain of RM25.44 million, after taking into account the reversal of deferred tax liability of RM4.47 million.
The group said proceeds from the disposal would be used to support working capital requirements, finance ongoing business expansion initiatives, fund prospective business activities and potentially support dividend distributions.
The group does not expect the disposal to have any material impact on its net assets, gearing, earnings or earnings per share for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026.
Barring any unforeseen circumstances, the disposal is expected to be completed by the first quarter of 2027.

Title: MACC remands brothers with ‘Datuk Seri’, ‘Datuk Wira’ titles over alleged RM10m investment abuse
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Two corporate figures, who are brothers, have been remanded for five days over an alleged abuse of position involving an investment of about RM10 million.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) obtained the remand order, effective today until October 5, from Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court this morning.
According to a source, the two men, in their 40s and 50s and carrying the titles Datuk Seri and Datuk Wira, were detained at about 9pm yesterday after giving their statements at the MACC headquarters here.
Initial investigations found that the duo were suspected of acting in collusion in the alleged offence in late 2020.
“They are also believed to have colluded with an officer of an education-based foundation to approve an investment of about RM10 million in an investment company owned by the elder brother,” the source told Bernama.
The MACC also seized 15 luxury cars, 12 high-powered motorcycles, five luxury watches, three bracelets and about RM30,000 in cash.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the matter when contacted and said the case was being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: Johor government to enhance ‘Smart City’ technology for early extreme weather warnings
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 1 — The Johor government will enhance its ‘Smart City’ technology to enable city residents to receive early flood warnings during extreme heavy rain that poses a risk of flash floods.
State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the early flood warning alerts or notifications would be sent directly to mobile phones via a smart application.
He said it was timely for such initiatives to be implemented so that urgent warning information could be communicated directly to the public, allowing them to take quicker action to safeguard lives and property.
“We need to gather as many mobilephone numbers as possible so that they can immediately start receiving notifications related to extreme weather conditions.
“In Japan, those within a 200 metre to 300 meter radius will receive an early warning notification due to adverse weather conditions.
“Such notifications also warn the public to avoid high risk areas or routes that are likely to be inundated by floodwaters,” Mohd Jafni told reporters at Menara MBJB here today.
Earlier, he chaired an action committee meeting with Johor Bahru City Council (MBJB) officials on the severe flash floods that struck several locations in the city yesterday.
Mohd Jafni explained that two flood warning sirens were operational during yesterday’s flash flood incident, with each sounding three times.
However, he acknowledged that the sirens may not have been loud enough.
“Yesterday, the alarm was triggered three times in Kampung Mohd Amin and near the Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA).
“The issue is that not everyone heard the sirens. So, there is a need to review the system and discuss it with our technical team,” he said.
Yesterday, several parts of Johor Bahru were inundated by flash floods following continuous heavy rain.
Among the severely affected areas were Jalan Ayer Molek, Jalan Yahya, Jalan Pantai, Jalan Wong Ah Fook, and Kampung Pasir in Tampoi.

Title: Johor rolls out additional RM30m after flash floods hit state capital
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 1 — The Johor government will provide an additional allocation of RM30 million next year to fund four urgent measures to address flash flooding in the state capital.
Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the allocation aims to fast-track the implementation of short- and medium-term measures to tackle flash floods.
He said the decision was reached following an action committee meeting earlier today in response to flash flooding that struck several locations in the city yesterday.
“Despite the Johor Bahru City Council (MBJB) spending over RM100 million to address flood measures in the past four years, the weather conditions can be very unpredictable,” he told reporters after an action committee meeting at Menara MBJB here today.
“At present we already have RM48 million allocated for flood mitigation projects for next year, that will be carried out in stages.
“The additional RM30m million allocation for next year will be used to aid existing issues that are not covered under the existing allocation,” he added.
Also present were Johor Bahru Mayor Datuk Mohd Haffiz Ahmad and Perling assemblyman P. Pannir Selvam.
Mohd Jafni said the four key areas of focus include the appointment of specialist consultants by MBJB to conduct a detailed study of the city’s drainage systems and aligning it with the comprehensive district-wide study being carried out by the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID).
“We will also construct underground retention facilities – specifically an On-Site Detention (OSD) system – along the Jalan Sungai Chat area. This involves excavating and building underground concrete tanks to store water, while the surface area can be utilised as a playing field or car park, similar to the project implemented at Kota Iskandar.
“Additionally, we will also increase pumping capacity towards the Johor Straits to manage exceptional rainfall over the next five years.
“In addition, the teams will also deploy mobile pumps to high-risk locations in the city,” he said, adding that the authorities will also upgrade and expand monsoon drains through the Public Works Department (JKR).
Besides the four key areas, Mohd Jafni said various immediate measures would commence by tomorrow.
He said these include deepening the retention pond in Kampung Mohd Amin and lowering existing water levels in ponds such as those in Taman Merdeka and Sungai Chat using a scheduled pumping system prior to heavy rainfall.
“These measures aim to create greater flexible retention capacity to accommodate rainwater runoff.
“At the same time, the integrated coordination involving MBJB, DID, JKR, and the district office would be carried out weekly to continuously monitor the progress of the various flood mitigation projects,” he explained.
Several parts of Johor Bahru were inundated by flash floods yesterday following continuous heavy rain.
Among the severely affected areas were Jalan Ayer Molek, Jalan Yahya, Jalan Pantai, Jalan Wong Ah Fook, and Kampung Pasir in Tampoi.

Title: Bidor petrol station shooting: Police record nine statements, hunt three suspects
Article:
IPOH, Oct 1 — Perak police have recorded statements from nine people, including the victim, in their investigation into the shooting of a businessman at a petrol station in Bidor Sentral last Tuesday.
Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said those whose statements were recorded included three family members who were in the victim’s vehicle, two people in a vehicle near the scene and employees of the petrol station.
He said the victim is now in stable condition after receiving treatment and undergoing surgery at Seri Botani Hospital, while police are investigating from various angles, including identifying the motive, which has yet to be established.
“So far, police have not been able to determine the exact motive for the incident. Once we establish the motive based on the investigation, we will announce it,” he told reporters at the Perak Police Senior Officers’ Mess here today.
Mohd Alwi said police suspected that three individuals were involved in the incident, including a driver, while the registration number of the vehicle used by the suspects was believed to be fake.
He said police had also obtained closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage from the petrol station, which showed the victim being shot from two angles, from the front and the right side.
“We also reviewed CCTV footage at toll plazas and elsewhere, but what we found was that they did not exit the toll.
“However, we are still examining various angles to identify the suspects,” he said.
Police are also investigating the possibility that the victim was being followed, based on the movement of the suspects’ vehicle, which was driven at high speed before stopping in front of the victim’s vehicle and opening fire.
According to Mohd Alwi, the victim is a businessman who owns a restaurant and runs several businesses around Bidor, Sungai Siput and Tapah.
In the incident, the victim, who sustained a single gunshot wound to the left shoulder, was sent to Tapah Hospital for initial treatment. — Bernama

In today’s proceeding, Mohd Adzrul argued that the Federal Court panel hearing the petitions should first hear the preliminary issue concerning the OIC before proceeding to hear the petitions. However, Petronas lawyer Datuk Dr Cyrus Das argued that there was no basis to have the legal status of the OIC determined as a preliminary issue and the OIC issue can be taken up in the course of hearing of the petition.
Senior Federal Counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly @ Arwi representing the Federal Government, supported the submission by Petronas’s counsel, arguing that its (Petronas’s) petition should be heard first.
Regarding Sarawak Government’s preliminary issue on the validity of the OIC, he said it was not necessary for the issue to be heard by way of a preliminary point of law and the state government can bring up the issue during the main hearing.
On March 16 this year, the Federal Court granted leave to the national oil and gas company to commence proceedings to challenge the legislative competency of the Sarawak State Legislature to enact certain laws and to declare several laws made by the Sarawak State Legislature invalid.
It claimed that the Sarawak State Legislature lacked the competence to enact, modify, amend or revise law with respect to matters under List 1 of the Federal List in the Ninth Schedule of the Federal Constitution.
The Sarawak Government, meanwhile, filed a petition against the Government of Malaysia and Petronas, seeking the Federal Court to determine the constitutional validity and continued applicability of several federal Acts to Sarawak.
The state government, among others, is seeking a declaration that the Petroleum Development Act 1974 (PDA), the Continental Shelf Act 1966 and the Petroleum Mining Act 1966, as applied to Sarawak, were unconstitutional and void ab initio. — Bernama

Title: Don't abuse your power, deputy IGP tells police
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 1 — Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) leaders have been reminded not to abuse their positions and instead carry out their responsibilities with integrity, accountability and fairness.
Deputy Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid said leadership was not a privilege to be used for personal gain but a major trust that must be discharged responsibly.
“Therefore, I urge that every decision made must be based on integrity, accountability and a sense of fairness,” he said at the handover ceremony for the Sarawak acting police commissioner and acting chairman of the Sarawak Contingent Persatuan Keluarga Polis (Perkep) at the Sarawak Police Contingent Headquarters here today.
Earlier, he witnessed the handover of duties from PDRM Management Department director Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah, who was also the Sarawak police commissioner, to his deputy DCP Saifullizan Ishak before Mohamad Zainal begins his duties at Bukit Aman.
Abdul Aziz also reminded leaders not to oppress or mistreat their subordinate officers and personnel, but to guide, listen to and protect those under their charge.
He said leadership based on such values was important in creating a fair, harmonious and respectful working environment. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s marine police nab 2,707, record 7,627 cases in national waters this year
Article:
PORT KLANG, Oct 1 — The Marine Police Force (PPM) arrested 2,707 individuals in 7,627 criminal cases in the country’s waters during the first nine months of this year.
Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA) director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said that the success was the result of continuous enforcement through various operations such as Op Taring Gelora, Op Taring Landai, and inter or intra-agency operations.
“From January to September, the team recorded seizures and fines worth RM525 million with the arrest of 2,707 people for various offences.
“The highest offences among them involve the Fisheries Act 1985 with 3,214 cases, the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 (428), the Control of Supplies Control Act 1961 (295), the Immigration Act 1959/63 and the ATIPSOM Act 2007 (213), as well as the Customs Act 1967 (189 cases),” he said at a press conference after officiating the 79th Anniversary celebration of the PPM at the Region One PPM Operations headquarters, Pulau Indah here today.
Mohd Yusri said that the success was also the result of effective bilateral cooperation and patrol coordination with regional enforcement agencies such as Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and the Philippines.
Commenting on the issue of illegal immigrant smuggling, he said that irresponsible parties use various modus operandi to infiltrate the country.
“They are targeting international waters by transferring illegal immigrants to another boat before making a ‘drop point’ to Malaysia, with the focus areas including waters around Perak, Selangor Johor, and the northern part of the Peninsula,” he said.
Meanwhile, Mohd Yusri said that PPM as a whole now has 22 projects under the Malaysia Plan (11MP to 13MP) worth RM1.064 billion.
“For future strategic planning, it involves the application of 19 proposed projects worth RM2.28 billion, including the construction of several operational bases for the team.
“PPM will also receive two aircraft carriers and five Fast Patrol Crafts, each worth RM100 million, to further strengthen the unit’s capability in ensuring the safety of the country’s waters,” he said.
Earlier at the event, Mohd Yusri presented the PPM 2026 Hero Award to Sub Inspector (B) Jakarta Makling, 72, in recognition of his contributions and sacrifices throughout his service in the force.
Jakarta, when met, expressed deep emotion over the award that was introduced for the first time since he joined the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) on May 28, 1972.
“In June 1976, while serving as a patrol boat crew member, I was involved in a battle with a group of armed pirates in the waters of Lahad Datu, Sabah, and was shot in the left shoulder.
“The bullet still remains in my shoulder to this day and serves as a testament to my sacrifice in carrying out my duty to protect the safety of the nation’s waters,” said the grandfather of 13 from Semporna, Sabah. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia plans A-to-D food grades to nudge manufacturers — and consumers — towards healthier choices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Malaysia could introduce a new food labelling system giving packaged food and drinks nutrition grades from A to D by the end of this year, Health Ministry official Dr Yap Wei Aun has said.
Dr Yap, chief executive officer of the Health Ministry’s Health Transformation Office, said prevention was a fundamental aspect of public health and cited the proposed labelling system as an example of the government’s preventive health initiatives.
He said the labels could help nudge Malaysians towards healthier food choices without relying on individual willpower alone, while also encouraging the food and beverage industry to reformulate products to make them healthier.
“At the population level, I’m a little bit less convinced that we can depend on willpower and education to really drive lifestyle change,” he said yesterday during the “Innovating for Retirement Wellbeing” panel session at the Employees Provident Fund’s (EPF) International Social Wellbeing Conference (ISWC) 2026.
Dr Yap said the Health Ministry had been working with partners, including the food industry, to introduce the “front-of-pack labelling” system, under which bottles of drinks or packaged food would carry an A, B, C or D grade.
An A grade would represent the healthiest option, while D would indicate the least healthy.
“So now does it depend on the person per se? Actually, the main effect of this is behaviour change happening at the industry level, in terms of reformulating these foods so that they meet the A and B criteria, rather than the C and D criteria.
“And then when these foods go out, you don’t even depend on consumer choice, prices, availability. The whole health environment has changed,” he said, adding that the approach would reduce reliance on public education alone.
“So, we were collaborating, there’s a terms of reference and a committee jointly with Singapore, because we realised that we share the same food environment. And hopefully this will be rolled out,” he said.
“So we are aiming for gazettement probably end of the year,” he added.
Dr Yap said the measure was among initiatives being developed to address major health risks including physical inactivity and mental health, as well as dietary risks in Malaysia involving “too much salt, too much sugar, and too much calories overall”.
Although the new labelling system may appear to be primarily a “consumer choice” initiative, he said it could work alongside other public health policies to encourage healthier lifestyles by changing the wider food environment.
“Imagine if you are a school — you can just decide we will only serve A and B in the school compound. If you are doing government procurement, if you are an employer, you are only going to make A and B available,” he said.
He said other measures could include restricting advertising for less healthy products and changing how food is presented in retail spaces.
File photo of Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad, whose ministry is developing a mandatory Nutri-Grade system to classify food and drinks according to their nutritional content. — Picture by Choo Choy May
Nutri-Grade in Malaysia and Singapore
While Dr Yap did not use the term “Nutri-Grade” to describe the front-of-pack labelling system, Singapore currently uses the term, which has also previously been cited by Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad in relation to Malaysia’s plans.
In a written parliamentary reply on October 27, 2025, Dzulkefly said Malaysia already had a voluntary front-of-pack food labelling system known as the Healthier Choice Logo (HCL), which assesses nutritional components including fat, salt and sugar content.
At the time, 1,002 food and beverage products had received HCL recognition.
In the same reply, Dzulkefly said Malaysia was developing a mandatory Nutri-Grade system based on sugar levels in drinks, which would be introduced in stages, beginning with ready-to-drink products before being extended to freshly prepared beverages.
Under the proposed system, Dzulkefly said advertising would be completely banned for drinks given a D grade — those containing more than 10g of sugar per 100ml — on any platform.
He said the measure was intended to encourage manufacturers to reformulate their products and reduce sugar levels.
Dzulkefly said Malaysia’s Nutri-Grade system was initially focusing on the sugar content of drinks because the National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) 2024 showed an increase in sugar intake among Malaysians, with more than half of free-sugar intake coming from beverages.
According to the World Health Organisation, free sugars include those added to food and drinks by manufacturers, cooks or consumers, as well as sugars naturally present in honey, syrups, fruit juices and fruit juice concentrates.
In Singapore, the
Nutri-Grade system
assigns drinks grades from A to D based on their sugar and saturated fat content.
Nutri-Grade labels are mandatory for drinks graded C and D, while advertising for products given a D grade is prohibited.
