Title: Three separate drug busts net RM3.44m in drugs, five arrests in Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 1 — Penang police arrested five people, including a couple, and seized various types of drugs worth RM3.44 million in three separate operations between September 21 and 27.
Penang Police Chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the raids by the state Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) resulted in the seizure of 8.83 kilogrammes (kg) of heroin, 15.06 kg of methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) powder, five litres of liquid MDMA, 182 ecstasy pills and 70 grammes (g) of ketamine.
He said in the first operation at 3.30pm on September 21, police arrested a 47-year-old local man by the roadside at Jalan Masjid Negeri, before questioning led them to a car parked nearby which was believed to have been used to store drugs and drug-processing equipment.
“An inspection found 8.83 kg of heroin, 5.35 kg of caffeine powder and heroin-processing equipment, with the total value of the seizure estimated at RM443,518.
“The suspect is believed to have obtained the drug supply from a syndicate before repackaging it for sale to buyers,” he said at a press conference at the Penang Police Contingent Headquarters here today.
The following day at about 8.50pm, police conducted two raids around Jalan Tun Dr Awang and Sungai Nibong Kecil, arresting two local men and a foreign woman, all aged between 27 and 42.
Lim said police seized 3.26 kg of MDMA powder and five litres of liquid MDMA, estimated to be worth RM1.2 million, while investigations found that the couple worked at entertainment centres and obtained the MDMA supply from a drug distribution syndicate.
In the third operation at about 11.30 pm on September 27, police from the Machang Bubuk Police Station arrested a 45-year-old local man at Jalan Seladang, Bukit Mertajam, and seized 11.8 kg of MDMA powder, 182 ecstasy pills, heroin and 70 g of ketamine from his car, with the total seizure estimated at RM1.8 million.
According to Lim, intelligence found that the five suspects were believed to have been active in drug trafficking activities in Penang since July, while the three syndicates were not linked to one another.
He said preliminary urine screening found all five suspects were negative for drugs, while checks showed that one of them, namely the first suspect, had previous criminal and narcotics records.
“Following the three raids, police also seized six vehicles of various types worth RM58,000 under the Dangerous Drugs (Forfeiture of Property) Act 1988.
“All suspects have been remanded for seven days to assist investigations, with the cases investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952,” he said. — Bernama

Title: F1 fever builds as PM Anwar takes pit-lane walk at Sepang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Formula 1 fever moved up a gear at the Sepang International Circuit today as Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim joined a Pit Lane Walk on the eve of the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
Video and photographs from the event showed Anwar making his way through the busy pit lane as teams carried out final preparations, with mechanics, equipment and activity around the garages offering a close-up glimpse of the race weekend to come.
He was accompanied by Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
The Pit Lane Walk gave guests a rare look inside the paddock and garage areas before track action begins from October 2 to 4.
This weekend’s race marks Formula 1’s return to Sepang after a nine-year absence, with the circuit last hosting a world championship round in 2017.
Interest has been strong, with nearly 100,000 tickets sold as of Wednesday — a record for races held at the circuit, according to Sepang International Circuit chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif. About 3,000 tickets remained available.
More than 200,000 spectators are expected over the three-day event, prompting Kuala Lumpur International Airport to advise racegoers to use public transport because of limited parking and heavier traffic in the area.
The circuit has also undergone final track works ahead of Formula 1’s return, including surface levelling to remove irregularities in the asphalt and cleaning operations to improve conditions.
Malaysia is staging the event under the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix banner following an agreement involving Formula 1, the FIA and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.

Title: Finance Ministry: Monthly SARA aid credited to recipients’ MyKad from today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Monthly Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) aid has begun being credited to recipients through their respective MyKad cards from today.
The Finance Ministry (MoF), in a post on X today, said RM100 in monthly SARA aid would be credited to households receiving Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR), while senior citizens and single individuals would each receive RM50 a month.
For recipients of both STR and eKasih, households will receive RM200 in monthly SARA aid, while senior citizens will receive RM150 and single individuals RM100.
MoF said 15 categories of goods have been approved for purchase using SARA, covering more than 140,000 essential items such as rice, eggs, bread, cooking oil, over-the-counter medicines, frozen food, canned food and school supplies.
SARA can be used at more than 14,700 selected supermarkets and grocery stores nationwide.

Title: Weather alert: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across KL, Putrajaya, Labuan and 10 states until 7pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Labuan and 10 states until 7pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the adverse weather was expected to affect several areas in Kedah, namely Kuala Muda, Sik and Baling; Perak, including Hulu Perak, Selama, Kerian, Larut Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk; and Kelantan, covering Kuala Krai and Jeli.
The same warning was issued for Kemaman, Dungun and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu; Rompin, Maran, Temerloh and Bera in Pahang; and Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Gombak, Petaling, Sepang and Kuala Langat in Selangor, reported Bernama.
In Negeri Sembilan, the affected areas are Seremban and Port Dickson, while in Johor they are Segamat, Tangkak, Muar, Kluang, Batu Pahat, Johor Bahru, Kulai and Pontian.
In Sarawak, the warning covers Mukah (Matu, Dalat, Mukah and Daro), Sibu (Selangau and Sibu), Kapit (Kapit, Bukit Mabong and Song), Bintulu, Miri (Subis), Limbang, Sri Aman (Sri Aman, Pantu and Lingga), Samarahan, Betong, Serian and Kuching.
In Sabah, the affected areas are the Interior (Beaufort, Membakut, Sipitang, Tambunan, Keningau, Tenom and Kuala Penyu) and the West Coast (Papar, Penampang, Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Putatan and Kota Belud).

Title: Health Ministry warns against GB Daily Glow Skin Cream after mercury found
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has cancelled the notification of the cosmetic product GB Daily Glow Skin Cream after it was found to contain scheduled poisons, mercury, and is no longer allowed to be sold in the country.
It said that mercury is banned in cosmetics because it can be absorbed into the body and cause damage to the kidneys and nervous system.
“It (mercury) can also disrupt the brain development of young children or unborn babies.
“It can also cause rashes, irritation, and other changes to the skin,” according to the MOH in a statement today.
Following that, the ministry urged the public to avoid buying and using the involved cosmetics.
Members of the public who are using this cosmetic are advised to stop using it immediately and seek advice from a healthcare professional if they experience any discomfort or adverse effects.
“The public is encouraged to check the notification status of a cosmetic product and the list of cancelled cosmetics by visiting the official National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA) website www.npra.gov.my,” according to the statement.
The statement said that the involved sellers and distributors of the cosmetics must immediately cease the sale and distribution of the cosmetics.
“The sale and distribution of this cosmetic are in violation of the Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984,” added the statement.
Individuals who commit an offence under the relevant regulations may be subjected to a maximum fine of RM25,000 or imprisonment not exceeding three years or both for the first offence, and a maximum fine of RM50,000 or imprisonment not exceeding five years or both for subsequent offences.
Companies that commit offences can be fined up to RM50,000 for the first offence and up to RM100,000 for subsequent offences. — Bernama

Title: Indonesia remains a favourite destination for Malaysians as August arrivals jump nearly 29pc
Article:
JAKARTA, Oct 1 — Malaysians remained Indonesia’s largest source of foreign tourists in August, with arrivals jumping 28.95 per cent year-on-year to 296,227.
According to Statistics Indonesia (BPS), Malaysian visitors accounted for 18.52 per cent of the 1.60 million foreign tourist arrivals recorded during the month.
“Foreign tourists visiting Indonesia in August 2026 were dominated by Malaysian passport holders at 18.52 per cent, followed by Australia at 10.75 per cent and China at 10.16 per cent,” it said in its latest tourism statistics released on Thursday.
BPS said overall foreign tourist arrivals in August rose 6.27 per cent from a year earlier, while arrivals from January to August reached 10.58 million, up 5.38 per cent from the corresponding period in 2025.
Meanwhile, it said Malaysia was also the leading overseas destination for Indonesian travellers in August, accounting for 32.64 per cent of outbound trips, followed by Saudi Arabia at 18.58 per cent and Singapore at 14.00 per cent. — Bernama

Title: Kuala Terengganu High Court awards RM47,000 to boy who broke leg after being ‘slammed’ onto chair by teacher
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The Kuala Terengganu High Court today awarded RM47,000 in damages and costs to a boy, now 13, who suffered a broken right leg in an incident involving a Quran and Fardu Ain (KAFA) teacher four years ago.
Judge Yusrin Faidz Yusoff allowed Muhammad Izz Anaqi Mohd Izwan’s appeal and set aside an earlier Sessions Court decision that had dismissed his claim,
Utusan Malaysia
reported.
The judge found that the lower court had erred by failing to properly assess the testimony of two eyewitnesses and a specialist medical report from Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital.
“The judge failed to assess the evidence of two eyewitnesses and the specialist medical report from Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital. The medical report confirmed that the pupil’s [the plaintiff’s] leg injury was caused by a forceful impact,” Yusrin Faidz said in delivering his judgment.
The High Court ordered KAFA teacher Ahmad Mursyidin Abdullah, 41, and his employer, Yayasan Islam Terengganu (YIT), to pay RM30,000 in general damages for the boy’s injuries and RM17,000 in costs, together with interest.
Yusrin Faidz also ruled that YIT was vicariously liable for the injuries suffered by the boy as a result of the teacher’s actions.
According to the statement of claim filed through Muhammad Izz Anaqi’s mother, Nor Azlina Mohamad Yasin, 41, Ahmad Mursyidin allegedly slammed the boy onto a chair at about 3.30pm on July 6, 2022.
The boy was unable to walk home after the class and was taken to a private clinic, where an X-ray confirmed that his right leg was fractured.
Muhammad Izz Anaqi, who is now a student at a Mara Junior Science College (MRSM), was represented by lawyers Mohammad Rafaei Adnan, Mohd Hazwan Hamidun and Alif Danial Ahmad Shahrulnizam.
Saifuddin Othman and Yuhana Junaidi represented the two defendants.

Title: Anwar thanks outgoing China ambassador for strengthening ties with Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today expressed his appreciation to outgoing Chinese Ambassador to Malaysia, Ouyang Yujing, for his commitment and contribution towards strengthening cooperation between the two countries.
Anwar conveyed his appreciation when he received a farewell call from Ouyang today.
He said Malaysia and China had built strong ties across various sectors, including the economy, technology, education and culture.
Strategic cooperation in areas such as the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL), 5G technology, artificial intelligence, ports and the rare earths industry had also opened up new opportunities for mutual benefit, he said.
“Both countries will continue to strengthen the longstanding friendship and cooperation between us, while exploring new areas for the benefit of our people and the peace and prosperity of the region,” Anwar said in a Facebook post.
During the meeting, Anwar said he also received a special gift from Chinese Premier Li Qiang —  a book about Hangzhou, which he recently visited and which is Li’s hometown.
“I deeply appreciate the thought and gesture,” he said.
Anwar undertook a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou from September 22 at Li’s invitation.
The visit focused on two main engagements — the WorldSkills competition in Shanghai and the Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou. — Bernama

Title: Selangor employers who chose Sultan’s Silver Jubilee Oct 25 holiday must observe it, says Labour Dept
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 1 — The special public holiday on October 25 in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of the 25-year reign of the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, must be observed by private-sector employers in Selangor who have chosen it as one of their paid public holidays.
The Department of Labour Peninsular Malaysia (JTKSM) said employers who designate Sunday as a rest day must provide a replacement paid public holiday on October 26 (Monday), in accordance with Section 60D(1) of the Employment Act 1955.
“Alternatively, with the agreement of their employees, employers may replace the paid public holiday with another day, in accordance with the Act,” it said in a statement today.
The department said the special public holiday was declared under subsection 9(1) of the Holidays Act 1951 [Act 369], which allows the state government to declare any day as a public holiday in the state.
On September 11, the Selangor state government announced October 26 as a replacement public holiday for the entire state following the declaration of October 25 as a special public holiday in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebration.
Selangor State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin said the replacement holiday was declared because the celebration and the special public holiday fell on a Sunday. — Bernama

Title: Nga Kor Ming offers one month’s ministerial salary for top Housing Ministry innovator
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming has called for every innovation developed by ministry personnel to translate into tangible benefits for the people by saving time and costs, optimising resources, and improving the speed and effectiveness of service delivery.
He said there is ample scope for innovation at the Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) as it oversees housing, local government, cleanliness and solid waste management, fire and rescue services, as well as urban planning, all of which have a direct impact on people’s lives.
“I hope efforts to foster a culture of innovation among KPKT personnel will continue to be strengthened and expanded, ensuring that innovation goes beyond competitions and becomes a consistent part of public service delivery,” he said.
He said this in his speech at the 2026 Ministry of Housing and Local Government Innovation Day (HIKPKT 2026) here today.
Nga said the ministry should expand, replicate and scale up proven innovations so they can deliver benefits on a larger scale.
Nga also pledged a reward equivalent to one month of a minister’s salary for KPKT personnel who win the Prime Minister’s Innovation Award, to further strengthen the ministry’s culture of innovation.
HIKPKT 2026, themed “
Memperkasa Inovasi, Memacu Prestasi, Menyejahtera Rakyat
”, showcased 54 innovation projects, including 43 Innovative and Creative Group (KIK) projects and 11 Minister’s Innovation Award (AIM) projects.
The Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) took the top two places in the AIM competition, with its BM Fighter team winning with the Checkpoint Tracker project and Sungai Bakap Strategic team finishing runner-up.
Penang JBPM director Mohamad Shoki Hamzah said Checkpoint Tracker was developed to help rescue teams locate people who get lost in forests, shortening search times and reducing operational costs and the number of personnel required.
“If someone gets lost in the forest, we can determine where they are. The team can then go directly to their location and bring them out of the area,” he said.
He said the system uses Global Positioning System (GPS) technology, an SOS emergency feature and a Progressive Web App (PWA), with hikers required to scan a quick response (QR) code before entering forested areas to enable their location and movements to be monitored.
Meanwhile, Puchong Fire and Rescue Station chief Muhammad Azizul Hakim Idris said his team’s Rescue Flex innovation combines three functions to address neck, arm and leg injuries, earning first place in the Department and Agency KIK category.
He said the innovation saves time and eases the burden on rescue personnel by reducing the need to carry multiple pieces of equipment during emergency operations, including accident response and search-and-rescue missions.
“The biggest challenge was developing a concrete idea capable of delivering a significant impact. With the support of the whole team, we were able to turn Rescue Flex into a low-cost, high-impact innovation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Something next week? Amirudin signals movement in Pakatan-Bersatu talks for Melaka polls
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 1 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) could see a development in its talks with Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia as early as next week, its election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said today, as the coalition weighs its options ahead of the Melaka state election.
Amirudin said PH remained in discussions with various parties and had not ruled out cooperation with Barisan Nasional (BN), with all possibilities still on the table.
“By next week, I think we may have something,” he said when asked specifically about the progress of discussions between PH and Bersatu, according to
Berita Harian
.
The Selangor menteri besar said PH’s immediate priority in the negotiations was securing electoral success, but stressed that any arrangement would also have to serve the interests of the people.
“For now, I see all possibilities as still open, and the door to negotiations also remains open.
“We are negotiating with all parties, but the priority is very simple. The first priority, of course, is victory for our side, and every party also has its own interests.
“Secondly, it is about the extent to which the interests of the people can be addressed through the coalition that we form,” he told reporters after officiating the opening of Sunway Medical Centre Damansara.
Amirudin said political stability would be another important consideration in deciding what form any electoral cooperation should take, arguing that it was needed to support economic recovery and allow the government to respond effectively to crises.
“Political stability must be a priority for every coalition that we want to form. The second consideration is what benefits it brings to the people, particularly how we want to help the poor, address housing policies and so on.
“Thirdly, of course, it must produce a situation that benefits all parties,” he said.
He added that negotiations should not simply be about winning seats, but should also take into account whether the parties involved could find common ground on policy.
“We are opening the space for discussions. At the moment, I appear to be receiving various reactions from leaders.
“However, as head of the election machinery, what I can confirm is that we are holding discussions and trying to reach decisions and solutions that can be accepted by every coalition involved. So, all possibilities remain open,” he said.
PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said on September 23 that no decision had yet been made on the form of political cooperation for the Melaka election and confirmed that discussions had taken place with Bersatu. He had tasked Amirudin with handling the negotiations.
The 28-seat Melaka state assembly was dissolved on September 23 to pave the way for the 16th state election. The Election Commission will hold a special meeting on October 7 to determine key dates, including nomination and polling day.

Title: RM35 nasi lemak, RM30 Indomie: F1 food prices rev up at Sepang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Formula 1 fans heading to Sepang this weekend might want to leave a little extra room in the budget, with a plate of nasi lemak and fried egg listed at RM35 on an official vendor menu for the race.
The same menu lists chicken rice at RM30, Indomie with a fried egg at RM30 and a serving of cut fruit at RM20.
For Malaysian racegoers used to finding those dishes at everyday prices, the figures are likely to be almost as eye-catching as the cars on track.
A group of four ordering the RM35 nasi lemak, for example, would spend RM140 before adding drinks or snacks. Four chicken rice meals would come to RM120, while four portions of cut fruit would cost RM80.
The prices are listed on a vendor menu circulated through the
event’s official QR ordering link
.
Sepang International Circuit is preparing for a packed Formula 1 weekend, with large crowds expected over the three-day event.
The Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia is also being pitched as a broader entertainment experience, with Bahraini food, culture and hospitality forming part of the attractions.
A Bahrain Village is among the features planned alongside the racing.
But for fans with a taste for familiar Malaysian favourites, some of the menu prices may provide their own race-day talking point.
With tickets, transport, merchandise and food all competing for a share of the wallet, spectators planning a full day at the circuit may want to check the menu before making their pit stop for lunch.

Title: Selangor Sultan marks silver jubilee with joyride flight for 149 orphans
Article:
SUBANG, Oct 1 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and Tengku Permaisuri Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin today treated 149 orphans to a special joyride flight to mark the Sultan’s 25th anniversary on the throne.
Their Royal Highnesses, accompanied by Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah, were welcomed at Subang SkyPark by Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
Istana Alam Shah, in a statement, said that the Kembara Semenanjung Joyride Flight, involving children from 29 orphanages, officially kicked off the month-long Selangor Sultan Silver Jubilee celebrations in October.
The children boarded a Batik Air Boeing 737 MAX 8 for a one-hour flight from Subang, flying through Penang airspace towards Langkawi before returning to Subang SkyPark.
The palace said the programme, organised by Tourism Malaysia and coordinated by Selangor Youth Community (SAY) and Yayasan Islam Darul Ehsan (YIDE), was intended to give the children a travel and flying experience they might otherwise rarely have the opportunity to enjoy.
“Exposure to new experiences, social interaction and outdoor activities is also hoped to boost their confidence and motivate them to continue moving forward,” it said.
The programme also sought to foster compassion, togetherness and greater public awareness of the welfare and well-being of orphans, while strengthening ties among participants, organisers, volunteers, agencies and the local community.
The palace said the programme also gave the children an opportunity to appreciate patriotism and develop a deeper understanding of the Selangor royal institution.
“The presence of Their Royal Highnesses and the Raja Muda Selangor reflects the royal institution’s continued concern for the welfare of orphans, ensuring they are also included and celebrated during this historic occasion,” it said.
For 13-year-old Amirul Mukminin Tahir, the flight was his first time on a plane.
“I felt a little dizzy, but it was fun, and I also got to meet new friends,” said Amirul, who is under the care of Pertubuhan Kebajikan Ar Rahmaniah.
Another participant, Adam Adliemie Haziq Abdullah, 14, said he was thrilled to meet the Sultan in person.
“Before this, I only saw His Royal Highness in books or pictures. I never thought I would get to see him in person. I was nervous too,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Singapore eye stronger business links to boost intra-Asean trade
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Malaysia and Singapore can collaborate to enhance business connectivity within Asean and boost intra-Asean trade by leveraging their strengths in supply chains, the digital economy, and key industries.
This was emphasised during the Third Annual Ministerial Dialogue between the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) and Singapore’s Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (Meti), which was represented by Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong, who is also minister for trade and industry.
Miti Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said both countries could explore ways to facilitate greater trade and business linkages among Asean member states, with the long-term objective of increasing the share of intra-Asean trade.
“Intra-Asean trade is not fully tapped. The total trade among the 11 countries in Asean is US$4.37 trillion, and among us Asean is only about US$800 billion to US$900 billion.
“There is much more we can accomplish, and I discussed with Singapore’s Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kin Yong the potential for enhancing business connectivity among all Asean countries. Our goal is to eventually see that 50 per cent of the US$4.37 trillion trade is conducted within Asean,” he told reporters here today.
Johari said the Asean Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) would also be an important strategy to strengthen intra-Asean trade.
He said Malaysia had proposed DEFA during its Asean chairmanship in 2025, and it was now important to move towards implementation and execution, with Singapore taking the initiative as the current Asan chair.
“It is Singapore’s turn to take the initiative, and we need to help them to make sure that we use DEFA as one of the strategies to further boost intra-Asean trade,” said Johari.
He emphasised that Asean could leverage stronger regional connectivity across almost all sectors, particularly supply chains and food security, as well as electrical and electronics (E&E).
“While not all industries are involved, a significant portion of our focus is on leveraging Asean for our supply chain, particularly in terms of food security.
“Additionally, there are many other areas where we can benefit from the strong connectivity that Singapore has to offer,” said Johari.
The annual ministerial dialogue between Malaysia and Singapore brings together government and business representatives to identify and address issues affecting bilateral trade, services and economic activities. — Bernama

Title: US$2m ‘scratch and win’ scam busted in Penang, 29 arrested
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 1 — Penang police have busted an international scam syndicate targeting victims, particularly in China and Cambodia, with the arrest of 29 foreign nationals in raids on three bungalows used as call centres in Barat Daya on September 22.
State police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the operation by the Penang Commercial Crime Investigation Department (JSJK), based on intelligence and surveillance, resulted in the arrest of 19 Chinese nationals and 10 Cambodians, aged between 20 and 63.
The first raid in Teluk Kumbar led to the arrest of 14 Chinese men who had no travel documents, while the second raid in the same area resulted in the detention of three Chinese men, a Cambodian man and three Cambodian women.
“The third raid at Solok Bukit Belah, Bayan Baru, saw two Chinese men and six Cambodian women arrested. Those detained in the second and third raids had passports, with some having previously entered Malaysia,” he told a press conference at the Penang Contingent Police Headquarters here today.
Preliminary investigations found that the syndicate had been operating for about two to three months, renting each bungalow for RM10,000 a month and converting the premises into call centres. The suspects were believed to have received up to RM8,000 a month.
The syndicate allegedly used Facebook Live and the LINE application to target victims in China and Cambodia through a ‘scratch and win’ scheme, offering prizes of up to US$2 million.
Victims were instructed to make QR code payments for processing fees, taxes and insurance, but did not receive the promised prizes. Initial checks found that the QR codes were believed to have been registered in Cambodia, with police tracing the flow of funds and other parties involved.
Police seized more than 200 mobile phones, 17 laptops, two desktop computers, six modem or router sets, customer records, ‘Scratch and Win’ cards, suspected fake documents and studio equipment believed to have been used in the operation.
Lim said police believed the three raids were linked to the same syndicate and were tracing its mastermind.
All 29 suspects have been remanded until October 13. The case is being investigated under Section 420 read together with Section 120B of the Penal Code, as well as Sections 6(1) and 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63. — Bernama

Title: MRT Corp: Overnight lane closures on Jalan Sultan Azlan Shah in George Town until Nov 30 for Mutiara Line works
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 1 — Long-term, periodic partial road closures on Jalan Sultan Azlan Shah here will be implemented from today until November 30 to facilitate construction work for the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) project in the area.
In a statement, Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) announced that the closures affecting the stretch from Sungai Nibong Bus Terminal to Batu Uban Road Transport Department (RTD) office will take place between 10pm and 5am to allow for tree cutting and relocation works.
“The closures will affect the leftmost lane between Lorong Sungai Dua 1 residential area and Batu Uban RTD office (towards Komtar), as well as the rightmost lane between Lorong Sungai Dua 1 residential area and Batu Uban RTD office in both directions.
“Additionally, the leftmost lane after the Sunny Point traffic light intersection up to Persiaran Batu Uban (towards Bayan Lepas) will be affected, however, other lanes will remain open as usual,” the statement read today.
Road users are advised to exercise caution when passing through the area. Signage, traffic cones, and flagmen will be deployed at the site to assist with traffic management and ensure the safety of motorists along the route. — Bernama

Title: MACC to take six anti-graft proposals before national governance committee
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — Six resolutions adopted at the Fifth National Research Conference on Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption (TIAR) 2026 last Friday will be submitted for consideration by the Special Cabinet Committee on National Governance (JKKTN) at its next meeting.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said this was to ensure the resolutions were translated into concrete improvements to the system, particularly efforts to strengthen corruption prevention, rather than remaining merely conference outcomes.
Speaking to reporters after the MACC’s 59th anniversary celebration and monthly assembly here today, he said one resolution called for the establishment of an integrated National Grant Governance Framework (KTGGN).
He said other resolutions included developing Government Procurement Regulations (Public-Private Partnerships) as specific regulations under the legal framework to strengthen the management of government concessions, as well as enhancing the eCOSS ecosystem through smart data integration to monitor cooking oil transactions.
Abd Halim said submitting the resolutions to the JKKTN was in line with MACC’s approach of strengthening corruption prevention through a more proactive, targeted and risk-based strategy.
In a related development, Abd Halim said the JKKTN, chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, meets three times a year.
He said the committee met today, but it could not table the six resolutions because the TIAR conference concluded only last Friday.
“So I think they may be tabled at the next meeting,” he said.
Meanwhile, Abd Halim said corruption prevention efforts should draw on investigation findings, data and risk analysis to identify areas that could create opportunities for corrupt practices.
He said Integrity Units should also be further empowered as strategic partners to management in addressing systemic weaknesses and identifying risks, so that breaches of regulations could be prevented at an early stage.
Earlier in his speech, Abd Halim said MACC’s efforts could not focus solely on action after an offence had been committed; prevention must instead be strengthened through an earlier, risk-based approach. — Bernama

Title: Penang man charged with secretly filming four women using factory toilet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — A 22-year-old man has been charged with secretly filming four women while they were urinating in a toilet at a factory in Penang, as well as possessing obscene videos.
Berita Harian
reported that Muhammad Mukhris Sulaiman pleaded not guilty to all five charges and claimed trial after they were read out before Magistrate Sharifah Razali at the Magistrate’s Court in Bukit Mertajam today.
For the first four charges, Muhammad Mukhris is accused of filming the women at a factory in Bukit Minyak, in the Central Seberang Perai district, between 11.44am and 6.55pm from September 2 to September 23.
The charges were brought under Section 509 of the Penal Code, which covers acts intended to insult a person’s modesty and carries a maximum penalty of five years’ imprisonment, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Muhammad Mukhris was also charged with possessing several obscene videos during an inspection at the Seberang Perai Tengah district police headquarters compound at 9.30am on September 24.
That charge was framed under Section 292 of the Penal Code, which provides for a jail term of up to three years, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Siti Nur Amalina Harun appeared for the prosecution, while Muhammad Mukhris was represented by lawyer V Sivakumar.
The court granted him bail of RM15,000 for all five charges and ordered him not to approach the alleged victims until the conclusion of the trial.
The case is due to be mentioned again on November 19 for the submission of documents.

Title: Nearly two billion e-invoices submitted by 268,000 taxpayers as of Oct 1, says Inland Revenue Board
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — More than 268,000 taxpayers have submitted 1.99 billion e-invoices as of October 1, the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) said.
Its chief executive officer Datuk Abu Tariq Jamaluddin said 196,031 taxpayers accounted for submissions under phase four of the e-invoicing rollout.
“The implementation of e-invoicing is being carried out in stages, with the government recently announcing an increase in the exemption threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million.
“This benefits micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), as businesses with annual turnover below RM3 million are no longer required to implement e-invoicing,” he told reporters after officiating the launch of ‘Bulan HASiL 2026’.
The revised threshold, which took effect on September 1, 2026, exempts MSMEs with annual income or sales of less than RM3 million from the e-invoicing requirement.
Abu Tariq said 5,582 taxpayers had submitted e-invoices under phase one, followed by 14,579 under phase two and 51,815 under phase three.
The e-invoicing system was introduced on August 1, 2024.
Meanwhile, he said IRB had more than 620,000 active corporate tax files and over 7.6 million active individual tax files as of August 31, 2026.
In his speech, Abu Tariq said Bulan HASiL, held under the theme “Voluntary Disclosure, Shared Responsibility”, provided taxpayers with an opportunity to return to voluntary tax compliance.
He said IRB had introduced several special initiatives, including the Special Voluntary Disclosure programme (PKPS) covering e-invoicing and stamp duty, as well as the Voluntary Income Tax Disclosure campaign.
“In brief, the PKPS e-Invois focuses on e-invoicing compliance, while the PKPS Duti Setem allows taxpayers to regularise their stamp duty matters with the benefit of penalty exemptions. The Voluntary Income Tax Disclosure campaign, meanwhile, provides an opportunity to correct income declarations,” he added.
One of the key activities under Bulan HASiL is the tax literacy roadshow, which is being held nationwide throughout October 2026. — Bernama

Title: Education Ministry halts school programmes involving freelance speakers amid allegations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek has ordered the immediate suspension of all programmes involving freelance speakers in schools following allegations circulating on social media involving a freelance speaker who had previously conducted programmes with pupils.
Fadhlina said she was aware of several allegations involving the speaker and had instructed the Education Ministry to obtain further information on the matter.
She said the allegations were serious as they involved the safety and protection of pupils.
“I urge anyone with information to come forward and lodge a police report. Reports to the authorities are important to ensure children receive the appropriate protection and support,” she said in a statement today.
Fadhlina said she had ordered all programmes involving freelance speakers to be stopped immediately to allow a full investigation to be carried out.
“Student safety must be taken seriously and scrutinised. The safety of children under our care cannot be compromised,” she said.
Her statement came after allegations involving the freelance speaker and school pupils circulated on social media.
The Star
reported that several alleged victims had come forward with accounts and purported evidence of inappropriate conduct involving the speaker.
According to the report, social media posts also alleged that the speaker had inappropriately touched pupils during programmes.
The allegations circulating online have not been independently verified.
Fadhlina said the ministry would obtain further information on the matter while urging those with relevant information to report it to the police.
She said reports to the authorities were important to ensure children received appropriate protection and support.

Title: ‘If the price is me, I’ll pay it’: Border agency chief Shuhaily ready to face action over viral KLIA incident
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said he was prepared to accept any action taken by the government over a viral video from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), saying he would take responsibility for what happened.
“I have informed the highest levels of the government and also the ministry about this matter. Therefore, whatever decision they make, I will accept it,” he said, according to
Utusan Malaysia
.
“For me, changing something comes at a price. If that price is myself, then I will pay it with myself.”
Shuhaily was responding to footage circulated on social media that appeared to show a man resembling him angrily confronting another individual at KLIA and holding the person’s head in a forceful manner.
A purported account from an individual claiming to have been manhandled by Shuhaily has also circulated online.
Shuhaily said he did not consider himself perfect and was prepared to face any consequences arising from the incident.
“I stand before all of you to face and take responsibility for what has happened,” he said.
He expressed hope that any decision taken by the government regarding him would not affect AKPS personnel, whom he described as the backbone of efforts to strengthen security at the country’s entry points.
Explaining the circumstances surrounding the incident, Shuhaily said he and other officers had been carrying out a limited enforcement operation on Level Five of KLIA after inspecting AKPS preparations for an expected increase in travellers ahead of this weekend’s Formula 1 race.
“The enforcement operation was also carried out following complaints about the activities of a foreign tout syndicate, as well as an increase in the discovery of drugs and contraband at baggage screening areas,” he said.
“During the operation, a foreign national believed to be involved in the tout syndicate was detained before being taken to the baggage inspection room.”
Shuhaily said two unidentified individuals then appeared and began filming while officers were interviewing the foreign national.
“When my officers approached them and brought them forward to see what had been recorded, they were instructed to delete the footage,” he said.
“I gave the strongest warning that the enforcement operation at the time involved only AKPS officers together with KLIA Aviation Security (AVSEC).”

Title: ICJ? Asean? Civil suits? What can Malaysia, others do about Indonesia’s choking haze?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Haze from Indonesian wildfires has blanketed neighbouring Malaysia and Singapore for more than a month, closing schools and sending respiratory complaints skyrocketing.
It is not the first time Indonesian haze has caused a regional pollution crisis, but neighbouring countries have few options for legal recourse, experts say:
Case at the ICJ
Suggestions that Malaysia and Singapore take Indonesia to the UN’s highest judicial organ, the International Court of Justice in The Hague, face a basic obstacle:
“The main issue is jurisdiction, as the ICJ generally requires the consent of both states,” said Professor Mohd Hazmi Mohd Rusli of Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia.
The ICJ can only hear a dispute where states have accepted its jurisdiction, for example through a special agreement, compatible declarations recognising the court’s compulsory jurisdiction, or a treaty clause referring disputes to it.
Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore are neither signatories nor parties to the 1979 Convention on Long-range Transboundary Air Pollution, a European-centred treaty framework intended to curb cross-border air pollution.
And experts agree Indonesia would be unlikely to willingly accept ICJ jurisdiction on the issue.
All three countries are parties to the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution, but the 2002 deal has no clause on litigation before the ICJ.
The city skyline is shrouded in haze in Kuala Lumpur on September 15, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
What about Asean?
The Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution is a legally binding regional treaty, intended to prevent and monitor cross-border haze from land and forest fires, and to mitigate its effects.
But its enforcement provisions are limited.
“It is legally binding, but it does not provide a mechanism for one member state to simply sue another,” said Hazmi.
Instead, it seeks to solve the problem through “national action and regional cooperation”.
Legal analysts say Asean’s emphasis on consensus, sovereignty and non-interference puts the brakes on how much diplomatic pressure can be applied to member states over domestic land management and fire enforcement.
“For now, I think the more practical approach is stronger Asean cooperation, including hotspot monitoring, information sharing, prevention and stronger enforcement against illegal burning,” Hazmi said.
Haze envelopes the administrative capital of Putrajaya on September 18, 2026. — Bernama pic
Civil action
One option could be for Malaysians or Singaporeans to try to sue companies linked to the fires in an Indonesian court, said Azam Hawari, a legal expert at the environmental law charity, ClientEarth.
However, “claimants would need to show a link between the company’s activities, the haze that reached them, and their losses,” Azam said, adding he was not aware of such a case having been brought successfully.
Added Hazmi: “Transboundary haze does not automatically mean Indonesia is internationally responsible.”
“There must still be sufficient evidence to establish the link between activities in Indonesia and the harm suffered in Malaysia or Singapore,” he said.
Previous attempts
Singapore enacted its own Transboundary haze Pollution Act in 2014, after pollution levels spiked into hazardous territory the year before, followed by another episode in 2015.
The law aimed to punish companies whose activities outside Singapore caused or contributed to unhealthy levels of haze in Singapore.
Enforcement proved a major weakness because it relied heavily on cooperation from foreign authorities.
Establishing responsibility was also challenging because it required authorities to share maps pinpointing fire hotspots, and conflicting or overlapping land rights could further complicate matters.
Bringing a case against some companies with no presence in Singapore also made collecting fines or damages hard.
People stand on the observation deck of the Marina Bay Sands on a hazy day in Singapore September 28, 2026. — AFP pic
Singapore’s investigations into four Indonesian companies over their alleged role in the 2015 transboundary haze remain open and proved a source of diplomatic tensions with Jakarta at the time.
Singapore will now most likely “wait for Indonesia to finger certain companies first before we take action against these same companies under the Act”, said Professor Alan Tan, an environmental law expert at the National University of Singapore.
“Otherwise, any action that Singapore takes would appear to the Indonesians to be unilateral, and could be politically controversial.”
Tan said: “Regrettably, not much has changed by way of how the root causes of fires remain unaddressed in Indonesia.” — AFP
